events.text: The miller stops calling {b3_clan} "that new lot up the hill". He says it the way he says the names of the old families, flatly, as a fact of the weather. Your youngest heard him, and has told everyone twice.

choices.text: Send the miller a sack of seed

effects.log: He sends back a sack of flour and no message. In this county that is a treaty.

choices.text: Tell the youngest to stop boasting

effects.log: They stop boasting. They start standing up straighter instead, which is worse.

events.text: A herald of the kingdom reads out the houses of the county at the spring fair, and {b3_clan} is on the list, eleventh, between a family of tanners and a family that owns a bridge. Somebody cheers. It is your cook.

effects.log: The cook is insufferable for a year. The food has never been better.

choices.text: Ask to be read tenth next year

effects.log: The herald says it is not done like that. It is done like that, you find out, for a modest gift.

events.text: They are carving names into the new lintel of the county temple, the houses that paid for its roof. {b3_clan} is cut in deeper than you asked for. The carver says the old priest told him to. The priest says the Maker would want it legible.

effects.log: You pray under your own name, which feels odd, and then less odd.

choices.text: Have the carver make the letters smaller

effects.log: He refuses on artistic grounds. The name stays deep.

events.text: A young couple from the next kingdom ask if they may marry under the eaves of {b3_clan}, because it is lucky now. Nobody can say when that started. The roof leaks in two places, and they would like to be married under one of them.

effects.log: You mend it the day before. They are a little disappointed. The marriage lasts anyway.
They choose the larger one. It rains. Everyone agrees it was very lucky.

events.text: Old people in the market have started to say "as steady as {b3_clan}", the way they used to say "as steady as the river". The river flooded last spring. You take it in the spirit in which it was meant, and then you check the levees.

effects.log: They needed it. Next spring the house is steadier than the river.
You enjoy it for a day. It is a good day.

events.text: Your eldest and your second cousin have not spoken for a year over a well. It is on the line between two fields. It is the only well. Both of them come to you on the same morning, each certain you will see sense.

effects.log: It costs a season and a great deal of digging. They both say it was their idea.

choices.text: Give the well to the house, not to either

effects.log: Neither is pleased. Both drink. The quarrel moves on to the fence.

events.text: An aunt who married out has come back, widowed, with three children and an opinion about everything in the house of {b3_clan}. By the end of the first week she has moved the kitchen.

effects.log: The meals arrive on time for the first time in years. The cook resigns, and is talked back.
She moves it again in the night. It is the start of a long and enjoyable war.

events.text: The young ones of {b3_clan} want a school of fighting arts in the yard. The old ones want the yard for drying beans. You have been asked to rule on it by both, in writing, which is new.

choices.text: Beans in the morning, forms at dusk

effects.log: It works. The beans taste faintly of exertion.

choices.text: Give the yard to the young

effects.log: The beans dry on the roof. The grandmothers never quite forgive you.

events.text: Somebody has been taking coins from the house box, a few at a time, for a year. Everyone knows who. Nobody will say it, because it is the cousin who carried half of them through the bad winter on his back.

choices.text: Say nothing, and add to the box

effects.log: The coins stop going missing. The cousin never says anything. He mends your gate that spring for nothing.
He weeps. It was for a debt. You pay it, and the box is left alone.

events.text: Two branches of {b3_clan} both want to name the new baby after the same grandmother. The baby has opinions too, mostly at night.

effects.log: The child grows up with a very long name and an air of compromise.
She names it after her own grandmother. Both branches are united, briefly, in outrage.

events.text: A son-in-law from the river kingdom keeps calling your house "the hill people" at dinner, as a joke. Nobody laughs any more, and he has not noticed.

effects.log: You take him fishing for a week. He comes back calling the house by its name.

choices.text: Tell him plainly, at the table

ok.log: He goes red, and apologises, and means it. The table breathes out.

fail.log: He sulks for a month and tells his own family you are tyrants.

events.text: The house has two seals, an old one and a new one, because of a fire forty years ago. Half the family uses one and half the other, and a magistrate has refused a deed because of it.

effects.log: The old ones are very quiet at the next feast. The deeds go through.

choices.text: Keep both, and write down which is for what

effects.log: It takes a winter and a ledger. It is the most useful book in the house.

events.text: Your grandchildren have formed a secret society. It meets in the hayloft, its oath is very long, and it has decided that you are its enemy, which is an honour.

effects.log: You lose three skirmishes and win the peace with honey cakes.
You are refused. You are made an honorary prisoner instead.

events.text: {b3_house} receives you in a hall with a dirt floor swept into patterns, which is how the old houses of this county show you they are old. The head talks about rain for an hour, then asks one sharp question about the people behind you.

effects.log: They like that. They tell you about the rain for another hour, warmly.
The head does not laugh. A grandchild behind the screen does, and the head almost does.

events.text: At the gate of {b3_house} a boy asks your name, the name of whoever raised you, and your business, and writes nothing down. He will remember it, he says, for fifty years. You believe him.

choices.text: Give a full and honest account

effects.log: He nods once. Inside, they are already expecting you.
He is startled, then pleased. He will remember that too.

events.text: {b3_house} serves you their tea, which is famous and terrible. The whole county knows it is a test. You have been warned. It is worse than the warning.

choices.text: Drink it, and ask for more

effects.log: The head looks at you for a long time. You are given the good tea next time.
Correct, says somebody's grandmother. Not brilliant. Correct.

events.text: You arrive at {b3_house} on the wrong day: a funeral. You are let in anyway, because in this kingdom a guest at a funeral is good luck, and you are given a broom.

choices.text: Sweep, and stay to the end

effects.log: You sweep. You stay. Nobody forgets who stayed.
It is proper. It is a little cold.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} is a woman of ninety who wants to know only one thing about you: whether you have ever been to the sea. She has not. She would like a description.

effects.log: She closes her eyes the whole time. When you finish she says, "Yes. I thought so."
She is delighted. You plan a trip together that neither of you will take.

events.text: {b3_house} is quarrelling with a neighbour over a boundary stone and would like your view, as a stranger, because strangers are honest by accident.

choices.text: Say where you think it belongs

effects.log: You are right, as it happens. Half of {b3_house} loves you for it.
They nod, disappointed. It was the safe answer.

events.text: A year keeping the accounts of {b3_house}. They have three sets of books, one for the taxman, one for the family and one that is true, and you are trusted with the third.

effects.log: You keep it true. Nobody thanks you. Somebody slips you the key to the good cellar.
You find a leak of silver in the second book. They are grateful, and a little afraid of you.

events.text: {b3_house} sends you with its wagons to the winter market across the pass. There are bandits, there is snow, and there is a mule that knows more than any of you.

ok.log: You meet the bandits on the high road and they think better of it.

fail.log: The bandits do not think better of it. You keep the wagons and lose a tooth.

effects.log: The mule takes a road nobody knew. You arrive a day early.

events.text: You teach the grandchildren of {b3_house} to ride. They are fearless, which is the problem.

effects.log: They spend a month falling. Nobody breaks anything all year.
One of them wins the county race. You are a hero, and slightly bruised.

events.text: {b3_house} has a feud with a cousin house across the river, and you are sent to carry a letter that is either an apology or an insult, depending on who reads it.

choices.text: Read it aloud yourself, choosing the tone

ok.log: You choose the apology. They accept it. The feud ends with a very large lunch.

fail.log: You choose wrong. You come back at speed.

effects.log: They read it as an insult. The feud continues, but nobody blames you.

events.text: A year guarding the granary of {b3_house} through a hungry winter. People come to the gate at night. Some are thieves. Most are neighbours.

choices.text: Open a side door for the neighbours

effects.log: The head finds out in spring and says nothing. Then gives you a field.
The granary is full in spring. The village remembers it was shut.

events.text: Up the path behind {b3_house} there is a hut with a smoking chimney. In it lives {b3_anc}, who founded the house ninety years ago and has not come down since the second flood. The family leaves rice at the door every morning.

effects.log: The next morning the bowl is washed and turned upside down. Somebody has noticed you.
Nobody answers. The smoke stops for a moment, and starts again.

events.text: The grandchildren of {b3_house} say {b3_anc} on the hill was the best fighter of three kingdoms once, and could still beat any of you with a walking stick. The adults tell them to hush, too quickly.

effects.log: They change the subject to the weather. That is an answer.
The children tell you everything, including several things that cannot be true. Some of it is.

events.text: You find {b3_anc} by accident, at a spring on the hill, washing a single cup. Very old, very straight, and looking at you as if you were a horse they were considering buying.

effects.log: The old one nods, finishes the cup, and goes. You feel examined to the bone.
You are permitted to carry the water. You are not permitted to speak.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} catches you on the hill path and says, very politely, that the ancestor is not to be disturbed. Then, less politely, that the ancestor is the reason nobody has ever taken this house.

effects.log: The head is relieved. You know where the hut is anyway.

choices.text: Ask why that would matter to you

effects.log: The head looks at you for a long moment and walks back down without answering.

events.text: The hall of {b3_house} is yours for the space of a breath. Then the door opens and {b3_anc} walks in from the hill with a walking stick, and every member of the house stands up at once, and so do you, though you do not mean to.

ok.log: It is the hardest fight of your life, and very short. The old one lowers the stick and says, "Well. Somebody had to."

fail.log: The stick moves once. You are on the floor, and the old one is already sitting in the head's chair, waiting for you to leave.

effects.log: You kneel. The old one says, "Good," and that is the end of your claim, and somehow not the end of your welcome.

events.text: Ninety years has not made {b3_anc} slow. It has made them patient. They wait in the yard of {b3_house} while you decide whether you are really going to do this.

ok.log: You win. The old one laughs, a dry happy sound, and goes back up the hill.

fail.log: You lose, and are carried out of the gate by people who used to bring you tea.

effects.log: You step back. The old one nods. "That," they say, "is how a house lasts."

events.text: The children of {b3_house} have run up the hill to fetch {b3_anc}, and here they come, the old one between them, holding the smallest by the hand. It is very hard to fight someone who is holding a child's hand.

choices.text: Wait until the child is let go

effects.log: The child is let go. Then it is very hard in another way.
You give it up. The children are disappointed. They wanted to see.

events.text: You are head of {b3_house}. On the first morning the cousins serve breakfast late, cold and in silence. It is a message. The porridge is also bad.

effects.log: You eat it. You thank them. By the second month breakfast is warm.
You burn it. It is the first time anyone in the house has laughed with you.

events.text: The register of {b3_house} has never had a name in it that was not born to the house. Your name goes at the bottom of the page, in a new hand. The old scribe will not write it. A granddaughter will.

choices.text: Thank the granddaughter in front of everyone

effects.log: She becomes your fiercest defender. The scribe retires to his garden.

choices.text: Ask the scribe once more, privately

effects.log: He writes it, very small. It is still a yes.

events.text: The first festival as head of {b3_house}. You are supposed to light the lamp at the gate. Half the family has stayed home.

effects.log: You light it for the half who came. Next year more come.

choices.text: Go and fetch the others yourself

effects.log: You knock on every door. Some open.

events.text: A cousin of {b3_house} tells the market that you only head it because the old head was tired, which is partly true. You can hear him from the stall where you are buying eggs.

effects.log: He does not know what to do with the eggs. He stops talking.
You agree loudly. The market laughs at him, not you.

events.text: Floods in the low fields of {b3_house}. Every family on them looks to the head, which is you, which is still strange.

effects.log: Thirty people sleep in the hall for a month. Nobody calls you an outsider after that.
You are up to your waist in the river for two weeks. It holds.

events.text: The young of {b3_house} want to marry into the next kingdom's houses; the old want them to marry the neighbours, as always. Both bring it to the head.

effects.log: Three weddings, two kingdoms, one happy grandmother and one furious one.
The old are pleased. One of the young runs off anyway.

events.text: {npc} arrives from {b3_house} with an aunt, a basket of pears and a list of questions in a careful hand. The aunt does the talking. {npc} does the looking.

effects.log: You answer them all. {npc} crosses off one, and smiles.
The aunt is scandalised. {npc} answers, slowly, and laughs at the end of it.

events.text: {npc} of {b3_house} has been sent to meet you and clearly did not want to come. {He} sits very straight and looks at the door as if it might rescue {him}.

choices.text: Say you did not want to come either

effects.log: {npc} looks at you properly for the first time. You both relax.
The orchard works. It always works. {He} stays until dark.

events.text: The match from {b3_house} is a widow named {npc}, a little older than you, who has run a mill alone for years and is not in any hurry at all.

effects.log: You spend a day being shown the mill. It is the best day you have had in a year.
The letter is answered in three lines. You read them many times.

events.text: {npc} of {b3_house} has a dog that has decided against you. {npc} says the dog is never wrong. This is going to be difficult.

effects.log: It takes a month and a great many scraps. The dog lies on your feet. {npc} considers this binding.

choices.text: Ask what the dog has against you

effects.log: {npc} laughs so hard the aunt has to come in. The dog stays suspicious.

events.text: {npc} has walked all the way from {b3_house} in the rain rather than ride with the aunt. {He} is soaked, cheerful and very hungry.

effects.log: You feed {him}. Everything after that is easy.
{He} keeps the coat. {He} brings it back a month later, as an excuse.

events.text: The roof of the house of {b3_clan} needs new thatch, and the whole family turns out on the same day, as families here do. By noon there are more people on the roof than thatch.

effects.log: The roof is done by dusk. It is the straightest thatch in the county.
Lunch is legendary. The roof takes two days.

events.text: A child of {b3_clan} asks who the Maker is, and why nobody has seen them. You find, to your surprise, that you have an answer, and that it is a strange one.

choices.text: Tell the child the Maker is busy

effects.log: The child accepts this and goes to play. You sit for a while.

choices.text: Tell the child the Maker might be anyone

effects.log: The child looks at you very hard, as if checking.

events.text: Every year the family of {b3_clan} walks the boundary of its land on the same day, beating the stones with willow sticks so the land remembers whose it is. This year you lead the walk.

effects.log: Your arm aches for a week. The land knows.
The children beat several things that are not stones.

events.text: A peddler offers to paint the family tree of {b3_clan} on silk, going back ten generations. You have three generations. He says he can invent the rest tastefully.

effects.log: It is a short tree. It is a good one.
He goes to the next house, which buys twelve generations.

events.text: A terrible harvest. The house of {b3_clan} has enough for itself and not for the village.

effects.log: The house goes hungry in a small way for a winter. The village never forgets.
It comes back in spring, every grain, with a jar of pickles.

events.text: Two of your grandchildren want to go to the schools of fighting arts in the city, and one wants to stay and farm. The farmer is the one everyone is worried about, for some reason.

effects.log: They all go their ways. The farmer is the happiest of them in twenty years.
"Somebody has to stay," the child says. You have to sit down.

events.text: The old family sword of {b3_clan} has rusted in its rack. Nobody alive has used it. It is still the first thing a visitor is shown.

effects.log: It is a very good sword. You hang it back up.
The grandchild cuts a fence post clean through and is grounded for a week.

events.text: A letter arrives for {b3_clan} from a cousin line in the far kingdom, nobody here has ever met. They want to visit. All fourteen of them.

effects.log: It is a loud month. Two marriages come out of it.

choices.text: Ask them to send two first

effects.log: Two come. They are lovely. The rest come the next year anyway.

events.text: A fire in the stables of {b3_clan} at night. The horses are out; the hay is gone; the youngest stable boy went back in for a kitten and came out with it.

effects.log: He is made under-steward at twelve and never lets anyone forget it.
He takes both with great seriousness.

events.text: Your oldest friend in the village asks to be buried in the family plot of {b3_clan}, though they are not family. The family is divided.

effects.log: The family grumbles. At the funeral, they all come.

choices.text: Give them a plot just beside it

effects.log: Everyone agrees it is fair. Nobody is quite happy.

events.text: A neighbour's goat has eaten the herb garden of {b3_clan}, again. The neighbour offers the goat as payment. It is the same goat.

effects.log: You have a goat. It eats the next herb garden too.
The goat respects the fence. The neighbour does not.

events.text: The young of {b3_clan} put on a play at the new year about the founding of the house. You are in it, played by a nephew with a beard made of wool. It is very unflattering and very accurate.

effects.log: You laugh the loudest. The nephew is offered a part in the city theatre.
There is a second act the next year. You come off rather better.

events.text: A matchmaker of the county says {b3_clan} is a good house to marry into now. Three proposals arrive in a week, all for the same granddaughter, who would like to be a carpenter.

effects.log: She builds the best chairs in three kingdoms and marries the matchmaker's son.
She chooses none, politely. She builds them each a chair.

events.text: The priest of the county comes to ask {b3_clan} to keep the shrine of the Maker on the hill, since the old keeper has died.

effects.log: Someone of the house climbs the hill every morning from now on. The shrine has never been so clean.
The priest takes it, but he is a little sad.

events.text: One of the cousins of {b3_clan} has been very successful in the city and has come home to tell everyone. In detail. For a month.

effects.log: There were several. The cousin tells them, and is liked much better.

choices.text: Put the cousin to work in the fields

effects.log: The cousin works one day, and leaves for the city with real respect.

events.text: The house of {b3_clan} has a ghost, or says it does: a grandmother who walks the kitchen at midnight and tastes the soup.

effects.log: The bowl is empty in the morning. The cat looks guilty.
You see nothing but the cook, eating soup. You never tell anyone.

events.text: Your first grandchild of {b3_clan} is born in the worst storm in forty years. The midwife says it is a sign. She says that about every storm.

choices.text: Name the child for the storm

effects.log: The child is loud, lucky and impossible to keep indoors.

choices.text: Name the child for the midwife

effects.log: The midwife cries. She delivers every child of the house after that, for free.

events.text: A stranger at the gate of {b3_clan} claims to be a lost son of the house, gone for thirty years. He knows the name of the old dog. He does not know your name.

ok.log: He is the real one. He went to sea. He has come home to die, and does not, for twenty years.

fail.log: He is not. He knew the dog from a story. You give him supper anyway.

effects.log: Real or not, he is the best storyteller the house has ever had.

events.text: The family argues every year about whether to sell the far field of {b3_clan}. This year an offer comes that would buy a new roof, a new well and a dowry.

effects.log: You sell it. The roof is very fine. The old ones visit the field anyway.
You keep it. It grows nothing much. It is the field where the founders married.

events.text: Late in your life, the whole house of {b3_clan} gathers for your birthday without telling you. You are made to sit in the good chair, which is very uncomfortable, for six hours.

effects.log: You sit. You cannot remember a better day.
It is short. Several people cry. The cook cries most.
